questions.q: According to this lesson, why does the story matter more than the code when presenting this capstone?
options: Neither an interviewer nor a manager is going to read the scripts line by line — both want proof you can turn something broken into something reliable
The code doesn't actually work, so only the story can be trusted
Interviewers are legally prohibited from reviewing code samples
Managers only care about the exact syntax of PowerShell cmdlets
questions.explain: The code is evidence; the story — the arc from a real problem to a real, measurable fix — is what actually gets remembered and evaluated.

questions.q: What are the four beats of the arc this capstone maps onto, in order?
options: Before (manual and error-prone) → automation suite → CI/CD → monitoring, tuned
CI/CD → monitoring → automation suite → before
Monitoring → before → CI/CD → automation suite
There is no particular order — any sequence works equally well
questions.explain: The order matters: leading with the pain point first is what makes everything that follows land as a solution to a real problem, rather than a solution in search of one.

questions.q: How should the same story be framed differently for an interviewer versus a manager?
options: An interviewer gets specifics and technical depth; a manager gets outcomes like time saved and risk reduced
A manager gets more technical jargon than an interviewer
Both audiences should get an identical, word-for-word script
An interviewer only cares about outcomes, never about technical depth
questions.explain: An interviewer is evaluating whether you actually did the hands-on work; a manager is weighing the business impact — outcomes and risk reduction land better there.

questions.q: Which single artifact does this lesson recommend having ready as a live demo?
options: The schema-change pull request from Lesson 39, showing the diff, review, pipeline run, and approval gate together
A screenshot of SSMS open to the Backup wizard
The original emailed .sql script from before automation
A spreadsheet listing every dbatools cmdlet by name
questions.explain: The pull request is the strongest single artifact because it visibly proves the process changed — a reviewed, auditable change instead of an emailed script.

questions.q: Why does leading with 'I built a CI/CD pipeline' alone, without the 'before,' weaken the story?
options: The listener has no way to judge whether the pipeline actually mattered without knowing what problem it solved
CI/CD pipelines are considered outdated technology
Interviewers are not familiar with the term CI/CD
It makes the story too short to be memorable
questions.explain: Without the manual, error-prone starting point, a listener has no baseline to measure the improvement against — the pain point is what gives the solution its meaning.
